title: Cached Wikipedia lead
description: One article's opening paragraphs as they stood at one revision, kept under tools/import/cache/wikipedia/ so a drafting run can read the same text twice and a reviewer can go and check it. It is somebody else's writing under CC BY-SA 4.0, not this atlas's: it lives outside data/, is never a record, is never published with the site (deploy.yml removes the cache before the Pages upload), and nothing in data/ may be a copy of it. The envelope exists so that the text always travels with the revision it came from and a link to the history that proves it.

lang.description: The language edition the text is from. Which edition matters: the editions are not translations of each other.

revid.description: The revision the text was taken from. Without it the cache is a quotation of nothing in particular.

historyUrl.description: The article's history, which is where the attribution the licence requires actually lives: the list of everyone who wrote it.

text.description: The lead section as plain text. Long, and deliberately not trimmed: a drafting run that reads half a paragraph draws worse conclusions than one that reads all of it.
